results.title: Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: 2026 Expert Consensus
results.summary: <jats:p>Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease that significantly impairs quality of life. Spasticity is one of the most frequent and highly disabling features of MS, often accompanied by cramps, pain, bladder dysfunction, sleep disturbances, fatigue, and tremor. Recently, the concept of ‘spasticity-plus syndrome’ (SPS) has emerged to reflect the interplay among these symptoms. This work aims to update the Spanish clinical guideline for managing MS-related spasticity (MSS) by adopting this evolving concept. Methods: A panel of 14 Spanish neurologists assessed the available evidence using a two-level literature review strategy, combining a systematic review focused on SPS with a rapid review of MSS management. Building on the previous guideline, the panel formulated updated recommendations with the scientific endorsement of the Spanish Society of Neurology (SEN). To support a structured and transparent development process, an adapted GRADE-informed framework was used to guide the appraisal of the evidence and formulation of recommendations. Results: A total of nine publications addressing the SPS concept were identified. Based on the evidence and expert consensus, the panel developed 13 recommendations covering triggering and aggravating factors, the diagnosis and evaluation of spasticity, and therapeutic strategies for patient management. In addition, a comprehensive treatment algorithm was proposed to guide therapeutic decision-making according to patients’ clinical profiles. Conclusions: This work provides updated recommendations for the management of patients with MSS, integrating the SPS concept into clinical practice. The panel highlights the importance of a symptom-oriented approach that considers the full spectrum of clinical manifestations to individualize treatment, simplify the therapeutic approach, and minimize the risk of polypharmacy.</jats:p>

results.title: Revisiting the MS paradox: automated 2.5D FLAIR segmentation and DTI microstructural profiling reveals dissociation between lesion burden and reference-like intralesional tract profiles
results.summary:
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
<jats:p>Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reveals macroscopic lesion burden in multiple sclerosis (MS) but correlates poorly with clinical phenotype, a phenomenon known as the clinico-radiological paradox. While diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics assess microstructural damage, standard whole-lesion averaging may obscure microstructurally spared white matter within heterogeneous plaques.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
<jats:p>We propose a fully automated, multimodal pipeline to identify and quantify reference-like intralesional segments (RLIS) within MS lesions (i.e., the cluster exhibiting maximum feature-space similarity to subject-specific, lesion-spared reference tissue). A modified 2.5D U-Net, developed and evaluated on a cohort of 75 MS patients (115 series), performed automated FLAIR lesion segmentation. In an independent cohort of 100 MS subjects, intralesional DTI metrics (FA and MD) were extracted along streamlines reconstructed via Constrained Spherical Deconvolution tractography. Unsupervised clustering algorithms, validated against a subject-specific, lesion-spared reference CST streamlines (internal capsule), identified operationally defined reference-like segments.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Results</jats:title>
<jats:p>The 2.5D U-Net achieved robust segmentation performance (DSC: 0.732, VC: 0.954), exhibited higher nominal metrics in a contextual benchmark comparison (DSC: 0.682, VC: 0.864). Across the clinical cohort, lesion count (11–131) and volume (0.54–57.3 mL) varied widely. Among the evaluated clustering methods, K-Means and Gaussian Mixture Models proved to be the most conservative, identifying median reference-like segment proportions of 26% and 22%, respectively. Crucially, the proportion of reference-like intralesional segments showed no significant monotonic association with macroscopic lesion volume or count.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
<jats:p>This automated framework successfully integrates robust deep learning-based lesion segmentation with tract-specific analysis to quantify the proportion of reference-like intralesional segments. The observed dissociation between overall lesion burden and RLIS suggests that this index serves as a promising candidate metric for exploring microstructural features that may contribute to the clinico-radiological paradox.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>

results.title: A Belgian study assessing relapsing multiple sclerosis activity through automated magnetic resonance imaging volumetry
results.summary:
Neurodegener Dis Manag. 2026 Nov 1:1-13. doi: 10.1080/17582024.2026.2752856. Online ahead of print.

ABSTRACT

AIM: This study assessed to what extent icobrain ms, a commercially available artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetry software, detected disease activity in patients with clinically and radiologically stable relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS), and estimated its impact on radiologists' assessments.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 111 RMS patients with two consecutive MRI scans at one year interval, without relapses, progression or radiological changes while remaining on stable therapy. MRI scans were analyzed by four radiologists acting independently, and by icobrain ms. The radiologists performed their assessments both without and with icobrain ms support and categorized patient status based on lesion and brain volume changes.

RESULTS: Radiologists' detection of lesion activity non-significantly increased from 6.8% to 8.6% (McNemar p = 0.215; ordinal regression p = 0.06; sign-test p = 0.08) using icobrain ms. Detection of accelerated brain volume loss increased from 2.0% to 7.7% (all p < 0.01). Inter-reader agreement improved from 36% to 56% for lesions, and from 26% to 40% for brain loss (Kendall's W, p < 0.001). Icobrain ms detected new or significantly enlarged lesions in 16.2% and accelerated brain volume loss in 6.3% of participants.

CONCLUSION: AI-assisted MRI volumetry may support radiologists to detect subclinical disease activity in patients characterized as having stable disease.

results.title: Computational identification of EBNA1-binding candidates using machine learning-based virtual screening and molecular docking
results.summary: Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) is associated with several malignancies and multiple sclerosis, and Epstein–Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) plays an essential role in viral genome replication and episome maintenance. The experimentally characterized KVD-associated pocket within the EBNA1 DNA-binding domain provides a structurally defined site for computational ligand prioritization. This study aimed to identify and prioritize predicted EBNA1-binding candidates using an integrated machine-learning and structure-based virtual screening framework. A PubChem EBNA1 bioactivity dataset comprising 304,124 records was curated to obtain 4,584 unique compounds. Molecular representation combined 1,024-bit Morgan fingerprints with 11 RDKit molecular descriptors. Random Forest, SVM-RBF, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost models were evaluated using scaffold-based independent testing. The optimized XGBoost model was applied to a non-overlapping DrugBank library of 12,287 compounds. Compounds with predicted activity probabilities ≥0.5 were subjected to Lipinski-based filtering, followed by molecular docking against the KVD-associated binding pocket of EBNA1 (PDB ID: 6NPM). Docking validation was performed by independent KVD redocking at exhaustiveness values of 8, 16, and 32. Post-docking candidates were further evaluated using PAINS, aggregation, frequent-hitter/promiscuity, assay-interference, redox-associated structural-alert, and ADMET assessments. XGBoost demonstrated the highest test-set ROC-AUC (0.835), PR-AUC (0.408), and best Brier score (0.067), and was selected for virtual screening. Screening identified 116 compounds above the probability threshold, of which 40 satisfied Lipinski criteria and were docked. Thirty-two compounds achieved docking scores ≤ −7.0 kcal/mol. Sequential liability assessment and integrated prioritization identified 10 computationally prioritized EBNA1-binding candidates with favorable combined machine-learning, docking, and structural-filter profiles. The integrated computational framework enabled systematic prioritization of structurally diverse predicted EBNA1-binding candidates for further experimental investigation. The identified candidates represent computationally prioritized molecules for subsequent biochemical and functional evaluation of EBNA1 binding and activity and should not be interpreted as experimentally validated antiviral or disease-modifying agents. results.title: Host genomic context determines the direction of an oracle-predicted sequence effect: a composition-preserving CpG intervention in Enformer and Borzoi
results.summary: Sequence-to-function models are increasingly used as oracles to score designed regulatory elements, on the untested assumption that an effect measured at one locus holds at another. Taking chromatin and host loci from multiple sclerosis risk regions, we kept four questions apart: sequence realism, transfer of discrimination, edit stability, calibration. A sixth-order Markov chain reproduced the cell-type-specific motif enrichment a trained transformer missed, despite its lower held-out likelihood. Scores differ in level between loci far more than between inserts at one locus, yet inserts selected by an Enformer-derived index kept 85% of their advantage at four unseen loci. Once GC was matched, however, the index separated peak-derived from inaccessible sequence at none of 12 hosts, and from random sequence in opposite directions at different hosts. Placing identical inserts and an identical CpG edit at 24 host loci, the effect varied far beyond sampling noise on host identity alone ($$\varvec{I}^{\varvec{2}} \varvec{= 95\%}$$), unpredicted by 18 host properties. It survives scoring only the bins the insert occupies ($$\varvec{I}^{\varvec{2}} \varvec{= 92\%}$$, and across 200 loci), so is no artefact of aggregation; the apparent host dominance, however, falls from 25-fold to 3-fold under that localised score, and the one locus positive under the whole-window score reverses under it. Borzoi reproduced the heterogeneity but not its amplitude, and the objective did not predict lentiMPRA activity. For these two oracles and this edit, the size of a predicted effect depends on where it is measured, and its direction at any one locus is not robust.

results.title: Real-World Classification of Pain States in Multiple Sclerosis Patients using Wearable Sensor Data and Ensemble Machine Learning
results.summary: <jats:p>Introduction: Pain assessment remains challenging due to its subjective nature and reliance on self-reports. These challenges are particularly relevant for multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, for whom pain is among the most common and fluctuating symptoms, occurring in multiple forms. Wearable sensors combined with machine learning (ML) offer the potential for continuous and more objective pain monitoring by leveraging physiological signals in real-world contexts. Methods: We monitored 18 MS patients over 48 h using the Empatica E4 wristband to collect photoplethysmography, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data. Physiological features were extracted from 5-, 10-, and 15-min time windows preceding hourly self-reported pain assessment during waking hours. Univariate associations with pain states were evaluated using linear mixed effects models, correcting for multiple comparisons. For classification purposes, feature selection was performed via recursive feature elimination, and 5 ML algorithms were trained and tested with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated using the F1 score and the sensitivity-specificity balance. Results: For univariate analysis, after correction, only 2 out of 43 features showed significant differences between pain and no-pain states. For the classification task, models based on 5-min windows generally performed the best. The highest F1 score (0.78) was achieved by a Support Vector Machine using 2 features from 5-min windows, while XGBoost achieved the best sensitivity-specificity balance (0.69/0.68) with 2 features from 15-min windows. Conclusion: Wearable physiological signals may contain information relevant to pain-state classification in people with MS. However, these results should be considered preliminary, requiring validation in larger, independent cohorts to establish the robustness and generalizability of the proposed approach.</jats:p>

results.title: Altered network organization with shift to local processing during adaptive behaviour in multiple sclerosis
results.summary:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
<jats:p>To adjust to changing environmental demands, the brain needs to organize and (re)configure mental resources in so-called task sets. Following a network perspective of cognitive functions, these processes are considered to rely on dynamic exchange of information between distant brain regions, possibly synchronized by slow-wave theta oscillations. However, few attempts have been made to describe the directional transfer of information in theta networks during behavioural adaptation. In the current study, we examined directed neural information transfer in 57 healthy individuals and 57 patients with multiple sclerosis with a focus on brain–behaviour associations during task switching. For this, we calculated behavioural switch costs and further applied an artificial neural network-based approach on neurophysiological EEG data to estimate linear and non-linear effective connectivity measures within cortical networks during task switching. Source reconstruction and connectivity analyses revealed distinct neural network architectures and communication strategies during task switching in healthy controls compared to patients with multiple sclerosis. In healthy controls, enhanced modulations of long-range fronto-parietal connectivities were associated with higher reaction time switch costs, possibly reflecting increased cognitive demands rather than adaptive processes. In contrast, patients with multiple sclerosis relied more strongly on local intra-regional modulations, which is consistent with the idea of a dysconnectivity syndrome in multiple sclerosis. Strikingly, stronger modulations in self-connectivities were associated with better accuracy measures in patients with multiple sclerosis, suggesting a compensatory mechanism to support performance. Notably, only non-linear directed connectivity measures were related to behavioural switch costs, emphasizing the importance of non-linear models for adaptive cognitive processes.</jats:p>

results.title: Digital Twins in Clinical Neurology: From Concept to Clinical Application in Multiple Sclerosis
results.summary:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
<jats:p>Patient digital twins (DT) are emerging as a promising paradigm for personalised and predictive healthcare. In neurology, and particularly in multiple sclerosis (MS), the availability of longitudinal, multimodal data provides a strong foundation for developing patient‐specific digital models, including simulation‐based and mechanistic approaches. However, it remains unclear to what extent current approaches represent integrated, clinically embedded DT systems.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
<jats:p>We conducted a narrative review to synthesise current concepts, modelling approaches and translational challenges of DT in neurology, using MS as an illustrative use case. Existing approaches were mapped to core DT components, including data integration, predictive modelling, dynamic updating and clinical integration.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Results</jats:title>
<jats:p>Current DT‐related approaches in MS demonstrate substantial progress across complementary development tracks, including multimodal data integration, predictive modelling, digital biomarkers, mechanistic simulations, virtual‐patient frameworks and in silico trials. These capabilities represent important building blocks of DT development but have not yet been fully integrated into continuously operating clinical systems. Core DT functionalities, including continuous bidirectional data exchange, real‐time model updating and closed‐loop interaction with clinical workflows, remain limited. Key challenges include data fragmentation, limited interoperability, lack of standardised validation, and regulatory, ethical and economic constraints.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
<jats:p>MS represents a highly suitable model domain for DT development. Future progress will depend on further maturing and validating individual modelling and data‐integration capabilities, as well as on their integration into continuously updating, clinically embedded systems. Robust validation, scalable infrastructures and appropriate governance frameworks will be essential to establish safe, effective and clinically actionable use in practice.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>

results.title: Fifteen-year real-world pharmacovigilance of multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapies: adverse event profiles, drug-specific safety signals and clinical implications
results.summary:
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Background</jats:title>
<jats:p>Disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) are the cornerstone of remission-phase management for multiple sclerosis (MS), a prevalent autoimmune neuroinflammatory disorder of the central nervous system. However, their immune-modulating mechanisms carry inherent risks of systemic and neurological adverse events (ADEs), which remain a major barrier to optimal long-term care. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the real-world safety profiles of all major MS DMT classes and identify clinically actionable safety signals.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
<jats:p>We analyzed 15-year (2009Q1–2023Q4) ADE reports for 8 classes of FDA-approved MS DMTs from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database. Four disproportionality algorithms (ROR, PRR, BCPNN, MGPS) were used for signal detection. Time-to-onset (TTO) analysis with Weibull distribution and multivariate logistic regression were performed to assess temporal risk patterns and patient-specific risk factors for important medical events (IMEs).</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Results</jats:title>
<jats:p>A total of 498,847 ADE reports (1,048,575 events) were included, with nearly 50% involving IMEs. The most common ADEs were systemic symptoms, infections, liver injury and alopecia. Notably, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML, ROR = 15.59) and spontaneous abortion (ROR = 2.54) were identified as high-risk severe events. Drug-specific analysis revealed distinct safety signatures: anti-CD20 antibodies carried the highest infection risk, natalizumab was strongly associated with PML (ROR = 45.62), and teriflunomide had the highest alopecia risk (ROR = 12.73). Approximately 70% of IMEs occurred within 2 years of treatment initiation. Multivariate analysis identified older age, male sex and longer treatment duration as independent risk factors for IMEs, while obesity was a protective factor.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>
<jats:sec>
<jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
<jats:p>This long-term FAERS-based analysis identified potential safety signals associated with major MS DMTs, providing hypothesis-generating evidence to support clinical vigilance and prioritize further validation, but not to estimate incidence, comparative risk, or causality.</jats:p>
</jats:sec>

Aubagio is used in the type of MS known as relapsing-remitting MS, when the patient has flare-ups of symptoms (relapses) followed by periods of recovery (remissions).

results.title: Identification of BRD4 as a Shared Diagnostic Biomarker Between Bipolar Disorder and Multiple Sclerosis Using Machine Learning.
results.summary: Bipolar disorder (BD) is closely associated with multiple sclerosis (MS), but their shared molecular mechanisms and specific diagnostic biomarkers remain unclear. This study integrated microarray expression profiling and machine learning to identify shared core genes and underlying mechanisms between BD and MS. Gene expression datasets and peripheral-blood transcriptome datasets were obtained from the GEO database. After per-cohort quantile normalization, shared genes were identified by differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed, and key genes were screened using the MCODE plugin. Three machine learning algorithms were combined to identify the final core gene. A total of 229 shared genes were initially obtained and further filtered to 55 key genes. BRD4 was identified as the final shared core gene. Discriminative performance (AUC, 95% CI) was: BD discovery GSE23848 (20 cases/15 controls) 0.713 (0.54-0.89); MS discovery GSE21942 (12/15) 0.998 (0.99-1.00); BD external GSE39653 (8/24) 0.775 (0.59-0.96); MS external GSE203241 (38/21) 0.828 (0.71-0.93). BRD4 shows moderate-to-good discriminative performance as a non-invasive peripheral biomarker and may aid further investigation of shared BD-MS mechanisms.
